scĭus , a, um, adj. scio,
I.knowing, having knowledge of a thing (mostly ante- and post-class., and rare for sciens, gnarus, peritus).
(a).
Absol. : neque quemquam invenit scium, Pac. ap. Prisc. p. 634: “mulieres plus sciae,” Petr. 63, 9 : “puto eos prudentes et scios mendacia defendenda suscipere,” knowingly, wittingly, Lact. 3, 24 fin. ; Vulg. Ecclus. 21, 18.—
(b). With gen.: “rerum,” Lact. 2, 14, 6 : “Latinae linguae,” Macr. S. 6, 9 fin.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
